name: Grassroots democracy
summary: Grassroots democracy is the principle that decisions should be made by the people they affect, at the most local level that can handle them, with power flowing upward from communities and members rather than down from a centre. Its advocates favour direct participation, assemblies and accountable, transparent representatives, and they build movements and parties that practise this internally. It is a view about how and where decisions are made rather than a full policy programme.
scope: The decision-making principle as documented in the Wikipedia article and its main advocates: the participatory-democracy strand of the Port Huron Statement (SDS, 1962), Ella Baker's group-centred leadership in SNCC, Saul Alinsky's community organising, the grassroots/participatory-democracy pillar of the Global Greens Charter and the US Greens' grassroots-democracy and decentralization values, and Bookchin's libertarian municipalism where it bears on assemblies and confederation. It excludes the rest of the Green programme (ecology, energy, trade, peace) and the rest of Port Huron's policy agenda; answers on those issues are low-confidence inferences from the programmes adherents commonly carry, capped at plus or minus one.

sources.title: Grassroots democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition: moving decision-making authority to the lowest practical geographic or social level; participatory versus representative axes; libertarian-socialist economic application.

sources.title: The Port Huron Statement (1962)
sources.author: Students for a Democratic Society (Tom Hayden, principal drafter)
sources.usedFor: Participatory democracy: individuals sharing in the decisions that shape their lives, politics as public problem-solving, decentralisation, democratic participation in economic decisions, student and faculty control of universities, nonviolence, critique of the party system.

sources.title: Charter of the Global Greens (Canberra 2001, updated Korea 2023), Participatory Democracy principle and Democracy section
sources.author: Global Greens
sources.usedFor: The grassroots/participatory-democracy pillar only: power concentrated in local and regional communities and devolved upward only where essential, grassroots institutions, access to information, equal vote, proportional representation, public election funding, multi-party system, local government, internal party democracy.

sources.title: Ten Key Values
sources.author: Green Party of the United States
sources.usedFor: Grassroots Democracy value (everyone has a say in decisions affecting their lives; accountable representatives) and Decentralization value (decisions at the individual and local level as much as possible; opposition to concentrated wealth and power).

sources.title: Libertarian Municipalism: An Overview
sources.author: Murray Bookchin
sources.usedFor: Face-to-face municipal assemblies over representation, confederation of mandated and recallable deputies who administer but do not make policy, municipalised economy rejecting both nationalisation and syndicalism, active citizenship, majority rule, opposition to the state.

sources.title: Bigger Than a Hamburger (Southern Patriot, June 1960)
sources.author: Ella Baker
sources.usedFor: Group-centred rather than leader-centred organisation, keeping the movement democratic, rejecting manipulation and domination, first-class citizenship, nonviolent principles.

sources.title: Rules for Radicals (1971)
sources.author: Saul Alinsky
sources.usedFor: Community organising: democracy as the best means to equality and justice, citizen participation as the animating force of a free society, trust that people with power will reach sound decisions, organising people where they are.

sources.title: Freedom Is an Endless Meeting: Democracy in American Social Movements (2002), publisher description
sources.author: Francesca Polletta (University of Chicago Press)
sources.usedFor: Scholarship on participatory democracy in SNCC, the New Left and later movements: bottom-up decision-making as strategy, and its fragility from aversion to rules and exclusivity.

sources.title: Participatory democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Theory (Rousseau, Mill, Cole, Pateman) and mechanisms: citizens' assemblies, sortition, referendums, town meetings, participatory budgeting, liquid democracy, e-democracy; criticisms.

sources.title: Subsidiarity
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The related principle that issues are handled at the most local competent level; Tocqueville on decentralisation as a counterweight to central power and a school of participation.

sources.title: Democracy
sources.author: Tom Christiano and Sameer Bajaj, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Participation as character-building (Mill), Schumpeter's elite theory of democracy as competition for leadership, and epistocratic critiques of mass participation.

sources.title: Libertarian municipalism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Bookchin's assemblies, confederation and rejection of both privatisation and nationalisation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Social-justice pillar commits to meeting basic needs unconditionally and treats public health as not a commodity; delivery by the state or by local bodies is left open.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Ten Key Values call for livable wages in a community-based economy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter wants prices to carry environmental costs and favors local self-reliance over unfettered markets, so adherents distrust the claim, though no stance on markets as such is stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter keeps water and essentials publicly controlled, but the tradition prefers municipal or cooperative control over national nationalization, so adherents split on the literal wording.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter seeks to close the gap between rich and poor and to break down inequalities of wealth that inhibit participation.

unions-good.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Organised workers fit the grassroots-institution ideal and the Charter cites fair labour and ILO conventions, though unions are not discussed as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter says it will review exclusive ownership against exclusive use and treats property as subordinate to ecological and social ends.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Both programs challenge corporate domination of government and want corporations bound by the strictest social and environmental laws.

cut-welfare.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Social justice pillar demands unconditional meeting of basic needs and strong safety nets, the opposite of cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Strands are split: some libertarian socialists want firms under worker or council control, Bookchin rejects worker-owned syndicalism for community custody, and Port Huron accepts accountable private enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter stresses civil rights and the Greens oppose curtailing liberties for the war on terror; surveillance specifically is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Grassroots democracy as a method says nothing on drug law and adherents differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Respect for diversity pulls toward restriction while civic-liberties commitments pull against; no stated position.

strong-leader.rationale: Ella Baker praised the student movement's group-centred leadership over a leader-centred pattern and warned against prophetic leaders with feet of clay; the whole approach distrusts a leader acting over people's heads.

state-harmful.rationale: Strands are split: Bookchin treats the state as a coercive force to be replaced by confederated municipalities, while Green parties seek to strengthen and democratise local and national government.

limit-guns.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. No source addresses guns; adherents are split between pacifist and community-self-defence views.

empower-police-military.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence pillar says security should not rest mainly on military strength and calls for disarmament.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter asks for economic security without recourse to prostitution yet defends sexual autonomy; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: The Global Greens' participatory-democracy principle wants power held by local and regional communities and passed to higher tiers only where essential, and the US Greens' decentralization value keeps decisions at the individual and local level as far as possible.

rehabilitation.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence and human-rights commitments imply a preference for rehabilitation; penal policy is not discussed beyond rejecting the death penalty and torture.

traditional-family.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter promotes equal rights regardless of gender and sexual orientation, which sits against privileging one family form.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter calls for recognition and respect of sexual minorities and equal rights for all, from which marriage equality is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter upholds women's right to decide on fertility without coercion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter supports separation of state and religion and a secular legal system.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter pledges to defend the rights of people of colour and acknowledges colonial exploitation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. No source addresses the metaphysics of gender; adherents divide.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Programs prize local and indigenous cultures and diversity rather than national tradition as such.

gradual-change.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter asserts need for fundamental system change, though through participation and nonviolence rather than rupture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Respect for diversity and equal citizenship rights point against restriction; migration policy is not specified.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Split: the Charter supports democratised global governance of multilateral bodies, while the local-first principle distrusts power moved far from the people affected.

free-trade.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter opposes new WTO-rules trade deals and wants labor and environmental agreements to take precedence over trade rules.

nation-first.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Personal and global responsibility is a core value and the Charter builds on global partnership.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence pillar rejects violence as morally wrong, though the Charter backs UN peacekeeping.

open-borders.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Greens favor equal rights for all and global responsibility but no program demands open borders; adherents split.

limit-growth.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter says continuing growth in consumption must be halted and reversed and rejects growth at any cost.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Global Greens Charter supports a rapid zero-carbon transition.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Ecological wisdom stresses living within limits; the Charter backs appropriate technology but not technological salvation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Global Greens Charter supports opposition to nuclear expansion.

revolution-justified.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence is a founding value and means must match ends, so revolution by force is rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: The tradition answers technocracy by giving everyone access to the information and education needed to decide, and Alinsky's core belief is that ordinary people with power make sound decisions.

central-planning.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Decentralization and local economies are core; centrally planned economy contradicts both.

socialized-markets.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Bookchin-style and Green views accept community-owned economic life; markets alongside democratic ownership are not explicitly endorsed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed by any source; Greens favor ecological taxes but no stance on land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Concern about concentrated wealth undermining participation implies support, though inheritance is not named.

basic-income.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Basic needs are guaranteed unconditionally per the Charter, but a state-paid basic income is not endorsed in the sources.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Local self-reliance favors protection of local economies but the Charter wants to avoid nationalist trade blocs; no stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. National-level direction of investment conflicts with decentralization, though green industrial policy is plausible.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Community-based economics and balanced local economies fit wide dispersal of ownership; not stated outright.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Programs ask for livable wages and do not propose abolishing wage labor, though libertarian socialist strands do.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not stated; Greens prefer democratic control of finance over market-run money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. State-recognised bodies setting wages conflict with bottom-up participation; not discussed.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Global Greens' participatory-democracy principle explicitly guarantees every citizen the right to join the party of their choice within a multi-party system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A hereditary head of state is not chosen by or accountable to the people, which cuts against the principle, though symbolic monarchies are rarely a priority target.

democracy-best.rationale: Alinsky calls democracy the best means to equality and justice and rests on the conviction that people given power will, over time, reach sound decisions even after mistakes.

direct-votes.rationale: The tradition wants citizens deciding directly rather than through distant representatives, but its favoured instruments are assemblies and grassroots bodies rather than national referendums, so agreement is moderate.

workers-councils.rationale: Split: libertarian-socialist strands favour councils, while Bookchin rejects workplace-based power in favour of municipal assemblies and the Greens work through parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Local self-government suggests sympathy, but Bookchin wants minority communities to defer to the confederation's majority on rights and ecology, so adherents are split.

natural-rulers.rationale: A principle that everyone affected should have a say in decisions leaves no room for a class born to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Port Huron calls violence abhorrent and seeks institutions that guarantee nonviolent conflict, and Baker ties the movement to nonviolent principles, though Alinsky-style organisers are less absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence pillar and disarmament goals reject war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter supports separation of state and religion explicitly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants a secular legal system.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants public, accountable institutions and a just secular legal system; privatised coercion is foreign to it.

military-superiority.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter says security should not rest mainly on military strength and pursues general disarmament.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter promotes multi-cultural society and equal citizenship regardless of ethnic origin.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Libertarian Marxist strands say so, but the mainstream Green reading does not frame history this way.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter seeks equitable distribution and equal opportunities, not literal equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter upholds indigenous rights to land and self-determination.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter speaks of an ecological debt owed by rich nations and calls for debt cancellation and compensation for displaced people.

civilizational-union.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Programs favor global cooperation and local autonomy over civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter prizes cooperation over competition and balancing individual interests with the common good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter couples freedom with responsibility yet affirms universal indivisible rights; duties are not placed first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Global Greens Charter supports respect for all forms of life.

limit-population.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants to halt growth in population but only by economic security and fertility control, not active state limits; adherents split on the literal wording.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter blames dominant patterns of production but does not call industrial civilization a disaster; green strands differ.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Precaution and limits are central to the tradition, opposing acceleration despite disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed by any source.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Decision-making by affected citizens is the core claim, which algorithmic rule displaces.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Civil society and openness commitments imply privacy backing; encryption is not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Programs seek system change and a new order, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed; the tradition's process focus is not clearly for or against pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Strands are split: Alinsky's organising and Bookchin's municipalism pressure institutions from outside, while Green parties contest elections as one route among several.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Global Greens pledge to model participatory democracy in their own organisation at every level, Baker stressed keeping the movement itself democratic, and Polletta documents movements practising the democracy they sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nothing in the programs supports it; they envision technology used sustainably within local communities.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not a stated aim; Greens accept specialised work and seek equal and decent conditions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants basic needs met unconditionally, though distribution by need is not made the general rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants an economy that satisfies needs rather than greed and rejects maximum short-term profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Libertarian socialist strands say yes while mainstream Greens only criticise profit-maximising; no stated position.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Dictatorial rule by a class contradicts participation, multi-party democracy and nonviolence.

collective-farming.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Bottom-up local choice is preferred to prescribed collectivization; Charter wants local food self-reliance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter blames financialised neo-liberal capitalism for inequality but does not claim an inevitable link to war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants taxes on speculation, carbon and polluting energy and public funding of services.

harm-principle.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed in sources; adherents split between liberty and community standards.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter upholds rights of indigenous peoples and minorities to culture and self-determination as well as individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence and demilitarization imply opposition, though no source mentions conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The tradition is built on voice, people taking part in and changing the decisions of their community, rather than on leaving.

state-as-business.rationale: Bookchin wants active citizens rather than passive constituents, which is the opposite of treating people as customers of government.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Charter makes access to education and the breaking down of inequalities of wealth and power preconditions for real participation, not just freedom from interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter worries about media concentration and corporate funding as the real power centres, not universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter affirms equality for all regardless of race and rejects racism.

organic-representation.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The model is direct participation of all, not representation by corporate bodies, though local communities matter.

total-state.rationale: Directing all of life from the centre is the reverse of devolving decisions to the lowest level possible.

national-rebirth.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nationalist palingenesis is foreign to a global, participatory, nonviolent outlook.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nonviolence and disarmament goals reject it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Equal-vote participation contradicts personal-loyalty hierarchy.

bound-labor.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter demands equal rights and fair labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. No source addresses it; critical-theory-influenced adherents agree while others do not.

universal-morality.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter claims universal, indivisible human rights, though epistemology is not discussed.

single-common-good.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Participatory process assumes pluralism of voices decided deliberately, while Charter also speaks of the common good; adherents split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed in sources; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed in sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter honours linguistic diversity and minority language rights, but state revival is not addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Port Huron Statement wants major resources and means of production open to democratic participation and calls for worker involvement in management, while accepting private enterprise that answers to social needs.

school-vouchers.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed; Charter wants education public and universal.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not stated; Greens back public investment for transition.

economic-freedom.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter ties democracy to equality and limits on corporate power, not to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Nothing supports rule by moral example of rulers; the Charter wants transparency and accountability of representatives.

national-self-determination.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter backs indigenous and minority self-determination but is wary of nationalism; adherents split.

force-without-un.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter wants to strengthen the UN as the global body for conflict management.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed; Charter respects spiritual diversity.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Universal rights and global responsibility imply extending basic provision, though immigration welfare is not discussed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter demands basic needs be met unconditionally.

class-collaboration.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed; Charter prefers cooperation to competition but also wants to break inequalities of power.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter protects human dignity and the value of cultural heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed in sources; adherents split.

workers-nation.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter favors international solidarity over nation-bound organising.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter's respect-for-diversity principle requires equality between genders in all spheres, which rules out legally distinct public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Not addressed in sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Charter rejects racism and calls for equal rights regardless of race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Libertarian Marxist strands say so; mainstream Greens see the state as reformable and democratisable.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. The Global Greens Charter supports a moratorium on new fossil fuel exploration.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Charter promotes multi-cultural society and the right of ethnic minorities to their culture and language.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from its preference for decentralised decision-making over central planning; the sources read do not discuss bureaucratic planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Split: Bookchin's confederal delegates are chosen from below by local assemblies, while Green programmes favour direct proportional elections for representative bodies.

national-church-status.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from its equal-participation and pluralist principles; a privileged national church is not addressed in the sources read.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the preference for decisions taken by the communities affected; the core texts do not discuss ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the idea that the people affected should decide matters concerning them; no core text addresses territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from its preference for community-scale self-determination over inherited state structures; not addressed in the sources read.

simple-living.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from the ecological-wisdom pillar favouring sustainable, limited consumption and local self-reliance; not stated as a rule.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from its respect for local community control and Indigenous rights; settlement limits are not addressed in the sources read.

equal-conscription.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle itself; inferred from the wider Green and New Left programmes many adherents hold. Inferred from its gender-equality and nonviolence pillars; conscription is not addressed in the sources read.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Not part of the local-decision principle and not discussed by its advocates; no lean follows from it.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed by grassroots-democracy texts; inferred opposition from the Charter's commitment to due process and proportionate punishment.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is outside the principle, and its advocates' texts take no side.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed; the principle concerns where decisions are made, not national kin abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed as such; some libertarian-socialist strands favour common resources but no core text states this compensation principle.

self-ownership.rationale: The core texts do not take up self-ownership, and strands of the tradition would read it differently.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax design is outside the principle and its texts take no position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The principle says nothing on targeting versus universal benefits.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The tradition depends on parties, grassroots groups and civil-society organisations, and Baker rejects movements built around a leader, so routing politics through one leader runs against it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred mild agreement from the Charter's pledge to challenge corporate domination of government; the principle itself is silent on business privileges.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not addressed by the core texts; no lean follows from local decision-making.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; the principle concerns decision-making, not technology or tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred mild agreement from the Charter's call to democratise gender relations; divorce law is outside the principle itself.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; local control is preferred to both national and foreign control, so the national-versus-foreign framing has no clear answer.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Outside the local-decision principle; the programmes adherents carry (Greens, New Left) lean toward equality, but libertarian-municipalist strands care about process, so they are split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Outside the decision-making principle; inferred from the Global Greens' and US Greens' programmes, which back taxing financial speculation to fund social and ecological aims.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Outside the principle; inferred from SNCC and Green social-justice commitments, which treat racism as a continuing obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the civil-disobedience tradition of SNCC and community organising, which acts against unjust laws; natural-law wording is not used in the sources.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Outside the principle; Green and New Left adherents are split between less work through automation and worries about control of technology and local jobs.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on decentralisation and power flowing from communities; no source addresses world order directly.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not part of the decision-making principle; adherents range from Marxists to non-Marxist Greens and liberals.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed; Port Huron and Green sources stress community and internationalism rather than national loyalty, and adherents are split.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from the Green and New Left programmes, which join social-justice and identity concerns with economic ones and do not subordinate them.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Party-led control from above contradicts the principle that power flows upward from communities and members, as the Port Huron Statement and Global Greens Charter state in favouring participation.

notes: Re-scoped 2026-10-21: the earlier audit treated the whole Global Greens Charter as grassroots democracy. Only the Charter's participatory-democracy pillar and democracy section are now used as stated positions. Strands split on assemblies versus elected representatives (Bookchin against Green parliamentarism), majority rule versus consensus, and municipal versus worker control of the economy.
